newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas to focus on broadcasting, publishing - Messier.
newsitem.headline: Havas to focus on broadcasting, publishing - Messier.

text.p: Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE), said Havas should concentrate on broadcasting and publishing following the accord between the two French companies.
He said in an interview with weekly magazine Investir, published on Saturday, that Havas had to get rid of conflicting interests among its own shareholders if it wanted to develop internationally.
"(Havas chairman) Pierre Dauzier and myself have an identical strategic vision. Havas should concentrate its development on broadcasting and publishing," Messier said.

"In the communication field the stakes are not just French, and if Havas had remained in its previous form, with fragmented shareholders and a board subject to conflicts of interest, its international development would have been compromised," he said.
Under the accord between communications company Havas and utilities to cable television conglomerate CGE, CGE becomes the largest single shareholder in Havas and will have five seats on its board.

Some other Havas board members have quit, including Jerome Monod, chairman of Lyonnaise des Eaux, which rivals CGE not only in its core water cleansing and urban waste businesses but also in its diversification into cable television.
Since the accord there has been speculation what asset sales could follow at Havas.
Messier did not discuss the future of Havas's travel agency Havas Voyages or advertising unit Havas Advertising, two subsidiaries frequently the subject of such speculation.
He declined to comment on rumours that weekly news magazines L'Express and Le Point could be up for sale.
"Those two journals belong to CEP, a subsidiary of Havas, which is run by Pierre Dauzier. It is therefore he who will put into practice the strategy of the group," Messier said.

He said the buy and sell option Havas and France Telecom have agreed on over Havas unit ODA, which sells advertising space in France Telecom telephone directories, was a sign that Havas is moving in the right direction.

"It (the accord with France Televom) values ODA at a satisfactory level, nearly three billion francs in the year 2000, and will give back to Havas its freedom in the field of telephone directories," Messier said.
